- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.7) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecast drop, it often overshoots; cap peak forecast at 10% below true peak.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day lagged trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 3–5% downward bias for first 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; match forecast slope to sentiment momentum.
